name: Okay I saw the nonsense you

messages.content:
Okay I saw the nonsense you did on the suspension rule you didn't follow my instructions. Implement the Jackpot Suspect Reveal mechanic in the existing game, following the existing game rules.

When a player uses SUSPECT after the opponent has passed their fifth card, pause the normal table interaction and trigger a short dramatic reveal sequence.

Suspected Player UI

Show a focused overlay/card:

YOU’VE BEEN SUSPECTED

“[Player Name] thinks you’ve got Jackpot.”

Below it, show the suspected player’s current cards.

The player must select exactly TWO cards from their hand.

Selected cards should slightly lift, glow, or scale up so it is obvious which two are selected.

The button remains disabled until exactly two cards are selected.

Then show:

REVEAL CARDS

When clicked, play a short card-flip animation.

Reveal Animation

The two selected cards should move to the centre of the screen.

Flip them from the back to the front with a quick 3D card-flip animation.

Only the player who made the Suspect should see the card faces.

Keep the revealed cards visible for roughly 1.5 seconds.

Then flip them back and return them to their normal position.

Do not reveal the rest of the hand.

Do not broadcast the revealed card values to other players.

Result

After the reveal, briefly show the result.

If the two cards are different:

SUSPECT FAILED

“Wrong read.”

Use a subtle shake/fade animation and continue the game.

If the two cards are the same:

CAUGHT!

“SUSPECT SUCCESSFUL”

Use a stronger success animation, such as a quick screen pulse, card highlight and small burst/confetti effect.

Award the existing Suspect point/reward.

Then automatically return to the table.

Keep the entire sequence fast. It should feel tense and satisfying, not like a long modal.

AI Suspect Response

When an AI player is suspected, the same visual sequence should happen.

The bot automatically chooses two cards according to its existing personality/strategy.

The human player who made the Suspect sees the reveal.

The bot should never reveal its entire hand.

Important

Do not redesign the existing table.

Do not create a completely separate game flow.

Integrate this into the current Suspect action and existing game state.

Reuse the existing card components, animations, styling and game UI where possible.

The experience should feel like:

SUSPECT → dramatic pause → choose 2 cards → FLIP → 1.5 second reveal → FLIP BACK → result → continue playing.

The mechanic itself remains unchanged:

The suspected player chooses the two cards. If they are different, the Suspect fails. If they are the same, the Suspect succeeds.
